extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of narratology; creative writers and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing or producing fiction using David Herman's cognitive narratology / storyworld theory, i.e., evaluating how a narrative evokes a mentally inhabitable world through situatedness, event-structure, worldmaking, and phenomenal experience (qualia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Storyworld (world evoked by narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The world evoked implicitly as well as explicitly by a narrative." A storyworld is not a list of events; it is a mentally and emotionally projected environment in which interpreters live out cognitive and imaginative responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the narrative evokes a coherent, inhabitable environment rather than only cataloguing events. Consider how implicitly as well as explicitly presented material contributes to the sense of a place/setting that readers can enter mentally and emotionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situatedness (discourse context / occasion for telling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative is situated in — must be interpreted in light of — a specific discourse context or occasion for telling. Every story is told somewhere, to someone, for a reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the strength and motivation of the discourse context: Why is this being told, to whom, and in what situation? Weak or unmotivated situatedness is a failure mode (the story's telling occasion is unmotivated). Consider whether contextual cues are adequate to orient interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event Sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative cues interpreters to draw inferences about a structured time-course of particularized events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge coherence of inferred event sequences: do the cues support a clear, structured temporal progression? Beware of mere accumulation of events that fail to constitute a sequenced, causally readable narrative (a 'chronicle, not a story').

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldmaking / World Disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative represents not just events but a world that the events disrupt and reconfigure; the reader builds and updates this world during reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the richness with which the narrative establishes the storyworld, and how events function to alter that world. Look for sustained internal consistency and meaningful reconfiguration rather than isolated incidents with no world impact. Failure includes events that do not prompt world-updating or contradictory frame cues that prevent world construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualia / What it's like (phenomenal character)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative conveys what it is like for someone to experience the events — the phenomenal quality of experience. Without this, you have a chronicle, not a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess presence and clarity of experiential perspective: does the text give access to sensory, affective, or perspectival qualities so readers can grasp what it feels like to be in the world? Absence of qualia is a decisive failure mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storyworld Construction (aggregate: frames, inference, affect, embodiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers actively build a storyworld using frame knowledge, inference, emotional engagement, and imagined embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or composing fiction, consider how these four building blocks operate together: whether frames are evoked appropriately, gaps are designably filled by inference, emotional hooks create investment, and imagined embodiment renders the world physically sensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame Knowledge / Schemas
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame knowledge: schemas about restaurants, weddings, hospitals, etc., that readers bring to bear to construct the storyworld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the narrative activates appropriate frames without over-explaining them; frames should support inference and worldmaking. Contradictory or missing frame cues hinder the reader's ability to build a coherent world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inference (filling explicit gaps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers fill explicit gaps in the text by making inferences; narrative should cue productive inferences rather than leaving incoherent lacunae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the text provides adequate cues for readers to infer necessary relations, motivations, and event consequences. Over-explicitness can stunt imaginative engagement, while under-cueing produces confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Engagement / Reader's Stake
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional engagement: the reader cares about what happens to whom; the narrative gives the reader a stake in outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the story generates affective investment through characterization, stakes, or perspective. A strong storyworld invites caring; absence of emotional engagement undermines inhabitation and the story's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagined Embodiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers sense the storyworld as a physical place through imagined embodiment—feeling or simulating bodily presence within the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree to which sensory detail, spatial relations, and embodied perspective allow readers to 'feel' located in the world. Imagined embodiment supports qualia and inhabitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The storyworld must sustain internal consistency—its rules, causal relations, and frame cues should not contradict one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for contradictions in setting, character behavior, timeline, or causal logic. Internal inconsistency disrupts worldmaking and prevents readers from reliably inhabiting the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure Modes / Anti‑patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which a narrative fails as a story: unmotivated discourse context; events that accumulate without world-making (chronicle); absence of qualia; missing or contradictory frame cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these anti-patterns as diagnostic criteria. If a text displays one or more, it likely fails to engage readers as a story. Examples: a list-like chronology lacking experiential texture; a story with no clear reason for its telling; contradictory setting cues that prevent coherent framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit Evaluative Criteria (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A piece of fiction can be assessed on: strength of situatedness; coherence of event-sequence inference; richness of worldmaking; presence of qualia/experiential character; reader's ability to inhabit the storyworld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compact checklist summarizes Herman's recommended evaluative dimensions—use it as an assessment rubric, scoring each dimension for how well the text enables storyworld construction and inhabitability.
